en: Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the ground, preventing you from slipping on wet bathroom floors.
Because water conducts electricity, touching a plugged-in appliance with wet hands can cause a dangerous electric shock.
Wearing light-colored cotton clothes reflects radiant heat from the sun, keeping your body cool during hot afternoons.
Listening to loud music through headphones for too long can permanently damage the sensitive hair cells inside your ears.
Looking directly at the sun can burn your retina, so always wear certified eclipse glasses to view solar eclipses safely.
Using a wrench with a longer handle increases the lever arm, making it easier to loosen tight bolts without straining.
Keeping strong magnets away from smartphones prevents the magnetic field from damaging the phone's internal speakers and digital compass.
Wearing a bicycle helmet protects your skull from the impact force when gravity pulls you down during a fall.
Eating carbohydrate-rich foods like rice provides your body with the chemical energy needed to run and play during school recess.
Wearing a seatbelt stops your body from continuing to move forward when a car suddenly brakes, preventing severe injuries.
Rubbing your hands together transforms kinetic energy into thermal energy, which helps warm your body during cold weather.
Turning off unused appliances stops them from transforming electrical energy into wasted heat, reducing the risk of house fires.
